value.intro: No cuts. No lost pay. The money comes from fixing the busywork.
value.proof: He's worked these jobs. He knows where the time goes.

rows.then: An agent answers every inquiry, gets a video walkthrough, prices the move and books the date. The office just approves.
rows.now: Office takes calls, books walkthroughs, types up quotes.

rows.then: Assigns crews and trucks, plans routes around traffic, re-plans when a job runs long, and texts customers live arrival times.
rows.now: Crews and trucks planned on a whiteboard.

rows.then: Crew photos and times become the invoice and payment link. Damage claims build themselves from before-and-after photos.
rows.now: Paperwork after every job: hours, invoices, claims.

examples.value: More jobs booked. Trucks stay busy. Paid faster.

rows.then: A phone video of the pool becomes measurements, a materials list, crew days and a price. The proposal goes out the same day.
rows.now: Every estimate measured and priced by hand.

rows.then: Orders the right amount from the best-priced supplier, timed to arrive the morning the crew needs it.
rows.now: Materials guessed and picked up in person.

rows.then: Watches the forecast and curing times, reshuffles the whole week, and tells every crew and customer what changed.

examples.value: Same-day proposals. No wasted trips. Owners kept in the loop.

rows.then: Tracks what sells, predicts busy days from weather and local events, and drafts supplier orders for a quick yes.
rows.now: Stock counted by hand, orders guessed.

rows.then: Builds shifts from the forecast and everyone's availability, and handles swaps by the shop's own rules.
rows.now: Schedules by hand, swaps lost in group texts.

rows.then: Takes phone and online orders, answers common questions, replies to reviews, and flags anything a person should see.
rows.now: Phones, orders and reviews juggled at the counter.

examples.value: Less waste. Shorter lines. The owner sees every day at a glance.

value.wired: Each one is a full system, wired into the phones, calendars, email and books the company already uses.

guide.title: Ask my agent

questions.a: He's going for Forward Thinking Engineer roles. He shadows people, builds them an AI agent and tools for whatever digital work they want automated, and teaches them to use it.

questions.q: How does a shadow day work?
questions.a: He spends a couple of days alongside someone, sees where their time goes, then builds tools for exactly that and shows them how to use them.
Anything digital a team wants automated, from small tools to full systems: quoting, dispatch, ordering, scheduling, paperwork. Built for them, not off the shelf.
Not yet. Everything here is his own project work.
A private research project that tests trading ideas on past market data. No real money, and no performance claims.
